regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Panitumumab + modified FOLFOX-6 is used for bowel cancer that has spread and has a confirmed wild-type RAS result. This NCCP regimen is a first-line option. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Panitumumab attaches to EGFR, a receptor on the outside of cells. This can interrupt signals that help some bowel cancers grow. A tumour RAS test helps identify whether this approach is suitable. EGFR also supports healthy skin, which explains why skin and nail changes need attention. Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected. Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself. Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.

regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Panitumumab attaches to EGFR, a receptor on the outside of cells. This can interrupt signals that help some bowel cancers grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Capecitabine tablets are given with pelvic radiotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer. The tablets help the radiation treatment work; your team confirms how this fits with surgery and other treatment.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: After you swallow capecitabine, your body changes it into fluorouracil. This interferes with the DNA and RNA processes cells use to grow. Normal cells can also be affected, which helps explain mouth soreness, bowel symptoms and changes in blood counts. Radiation is directed at the planned area. Capecitabine helps sensitise cancer cells to it. Nearby bowel, bladder and skin may also become irritated. Effects can build over the weeks and may continue after the final session.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–5 of each 7-day cycle, alongside radiotherapy, for up to 5–6 cycles. Follow the written plan for treatment days and interruptions.
key_points: DPD assessment before capecitabine
Current toxicity and recurrence guide different decisions
Unentered values remain unassessed
Radiotherapy schedule and medical oncology decisions require coordination

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Capecitabine tablets are given with pelvic radiotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer. The tablets help the radiation treatment work; your team confirms how this fits with surgery and other treatment.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Use the exact NCCP indication; DPD testing is a safety assessment, not a tumour biomarker.

important_cautions: Complete DPD deficiency, severe prior fluoropyrimidine reaction, relevant hypersensitivity and pregnancy/lactation are exclusions.
Brivudine requires avoidance and an interval of at least four weeks before capecitabine.
The renal table differs between 00623 and 00216/00586; do not transplant dose rules.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Capecitabine: oral minimal-to-low risk. Radiotherapy-associated nausea depends on site and field and needs the radiation oncology plan. Follow local policy; provide rescue treatment and stop-and-call education.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the oral minimal-to-low antiemetic pathway and individual rescue plan; no parenteral prescription is inferred.
Give a written diarrhoea, oral-care and hand-foot management plan.
patient_education: Ask for the number of each tablet strength per dose, the start and stop days, and the contact number. This page does not calculate a personal dose.
Skip that dose; take the next scheduled dose at its usual time unless the team has told you to stop. Never double up. Record missed doses and report repeated vomiting.
Use the agreed skin and mouth-care plan. Keep your prescribed anti-sickness and diarrhoea medicines available. Significant symptoms still require stopping tablets and calling.
Confirm DPD testing and regular blood tests. Tell the team about warfarin, phenytoin, allopurinol, brivudine and any new medicines or supplements. These need an interaction check.
special_support: Assess hydration, nutrition, frailty and ability to manage the tablet regimen.
G-CSF is not presented as a routine fixed prescription; assess febrile-neutropenia risk and local primary/secondary prophylaxis policy individually.

Attend radiotherapy planning and treatment appointments. Follow the centre’s bladder/bowel preparation instructions; ask how bank holidays or a missed session affect tablets.
Take the prescribed morning and evening doses with or within 30 minutes of food, swallowed whole with water. If swallowing is difficult, contact pharmacy for a safe plan.

drug_profiles.name: Panitumumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds the extracellular domain of EGFR and inhibits receptor signalling. Extended RAS wild-type tumour status is required for the NCCP colorectal indications. EGFR activity in healthy tissues helps explain skin and nail toxicity.
